title: How Tibo shipped a product a week to find Tweet Hunter and what he learned
summary: Tibo recounts how two failed early startups taught him to validate with payments, build hands-on, and ship fast. He then describes shipping one product a week until Tweet Hunter took off, and how a viral partner launch drove growth to an acquisition.

principles.text: Ship a new product every week and collect feedback until one sticks.
principles.quote: we would try to ship um one new product every week until something stick. uh it was early 2021 and I think in four months we shipped something like 10 or 11 projects.

principles.text: Validate demand through payments, not free usage. Going free only proves people will use it for nothing.
principles.quote: The validation comes from the payments. Meaning like if people pay, I get my product validated, but I want to prove that people are willing to pay for it and not even use it for free.

principles.text: Don't delegate the hard startup work; staying hands-on with product and marketing is what matters.
principles.quote: I was basically u delegating the most difficult task of a startup which is creating the product, understanding what people want and and even marketing the product.

principles.text: Fix your own problem: you are the expert on it, and many others likely share it.
principles.quote: try to fix your own issue. You you are basically an expert on your own problems, you understand them better than anyone else.

principles.text: Build what people actually want, not how you wish the world worked.
principles.quote: the product that works, they do what people want. They do not do what the founder would like the world to work that way.

principles.text: Growth comes from relentless daily shipping and talking to users, not a single big move.
principles.quote: almost every day we were adding a few features, almost every week we were shipping um a free tool to try to rank on some SEO keywords.
